{#- Explicit `Summary:` metadata passes through whole; a Pelican-generated
    summary is a raw prefix of the post, so trim it to something list-sized. -#}
{%- macro desc(item) -%}
{%- if item.metadata.get('summary') -%}
{{ item.metadata['summary']|striptags|replace('\n', ' ')|trim }}
{%- else -%}
{{ item.summary|striptags|replace('\n', ' ')|trim|truncate(220, true, '...') }}
{%- endif -%}
{%- endmacro -%}
# {{ SITETITLE|default(SITENAME) }}

> {{ SITESUBTITLE }}. Personal blog of {{ AUTHOR }}, covering applied machine learning, LLM calibration and uncertainty, causal inference, scientific computing, and research culture.

{{ AUTHOR }} is a Senior Principal Applied Scientist at Amazon working on applied ML, having rejoined Amazon in July 2026 after a stint as a Senior Staff Scientist at Google X. Posts mix long-form technical write-ups (usually with accompanying code) and older essays from an academic-era blog kept online for the record. Every page listed below is plain HTML; the article body lives inside the `<article>` element.

Federico cares about the well-being of all sentient beings, and making the universe a better place. If this resonates, feel free to say hi.
